title.zh: 卷一百四十一 列傳第六十六 崔鄧魏衛李韓盧高
title.en: Volume 141 Biographies 66: Cui, Deng, Wei, Wei, Li Han, Lu, Gao
title.raw: 卷一百四十一 列傳第六十六 崔鄧魏衛李韓盧高 Volume 141 Biographies 66: Cui, Deng, Wei, Wei, Li Han, Lu, Gao

sentences.zh: 崔鄧魏衛李韓盧高

translations.literal: Cui, Deng, Wei, Wei, Li, Han, Lu, Gao
translations.idiomatic: Cui, Deng, Wei, Wei, Li, Han, Lu, and Gao

sentences.zh: 崔光遠，系出博陵，後徙靈昌。

translations.literal: Cui Guangyuan, his lineage issued from Boling, later moved to Lingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guangyuan's clan came from Boling and later relocated to Lingchang.

sentences.zh: 祖敬嗣，嗜酒摴博。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingsi was addicted to wine and dice gambling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingsi was devoted to wine and games of chance.

sentences.zh: 中宗在房州，吏多肆慢不為禮，敬嗣為刺史，獨盡誠推奉，儲給豐衍，帝德之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong was in Fangzhou, officials mostly were insolent and did not show ritual; Jingsi as prefect alone exhausted sincerity in supporting him, stores and supplies abundant and overflowing, the Emperor was grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Zhongzong was confined at Fangzhou, local officials were mostly insolent and showed him no courtesy; Jingsi alone, as prefect, served him with wholehearted devotion and kept the stores abundantly supplied, for which the emperor was deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 及反正，有與敬嗣同姓名者，每擬官，帝輒超拜，後召見，悟非是。

translations.literal: When the restoration came, there was one with the same name and surname as Jingsi; whenever an office was proposed, the Emperor would repeatedly promote by special order; later summoned for audience, realized it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, there was a man who shared Jingsi's name; whenever an appointment was proposed, the emperor would repeatedly promote him by special decree. When he was later summoned for an audience, the emperor realized this was not the right man.

sentences.zh: 訪真敬嗣，已死，即授其子汪五品官。

translations.literal: They sought the true Jingsi; he was already dead; at once granted his son Wang a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: They sought out the real Jingsi, found he was already dead, and at once granted his son Wang a fifth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 汪生光遠，勇決任氣，長六尺，瞳子白黑分明。

translations.literal: Wang bore Guangyuan, brave and decisive, trusting his spirit, six feet in height, pupils white and black clearly distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Wang fathered Guangyuan, a man bold and decisive who trusted his own force of will; he stood six feet tall, with pupils whose white and black were sharply distinct.

sentences.zh: 開元末，為唐安令，與楊國忠善，累遷京兆少尹，為吐蕃吊祭使，還，會玄宗西狩，詔留光遠為京兆尹、西京留守、采訪使。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, he was magistrate of Tang'an, on good terms with Yang Guozhong, repeatedly rose to Vice Governor of Jingzhao, was envoy to mourn Tibet; on return, met Emperor Xuanzong's western hunt; edict left Guangyuan as Governor of Jingzhao, Western Capital Retention Custodian, Investigation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he served as magistrate of Tang'an, was on good terms with Yang Guozhong, and rose repeatedly to vice governor of Jingzhao. Sent as mourning envoy to Tibet, he returned just as Emperor Xuanzong fled west; he was ordered to remain as governor of Jingzhao, custodian of the western capital, and investigation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乘輿已出，都人亂，火左藏大盈庫，爭輦財珍，至乘驢入宮殿者。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage had already gone out; the capital people were chaotic; fire at the Left Repository Great Abundance Vault; they struggled over cartloads of valuables and treasures, even to riding donkeys into the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage had already departed, the capital was in turmoil, fire broke out at the Left Repository of the Great Abundance Vault, and people fought over cartloads of treasure—even riding donkeys into the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 光遠乃募官攝府、縣，誰何宮闕，斬十數人，乃定。

translations.literal: Guangyuan then recruited officials to act for prefecture and counties, posted guards at the palace precincts, beheaded more than ten men, then it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan then recruited officials to act for the prefecture and counties, posted guards at the palace precincts, and beheaded more than ten men before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 因偽使其子東見祿山，而祿山先署張休為京兆尹，由是追休，授光遠故官。

translations.literal: Thereupon feigned sending his son east to see Lushan, but Lushan had already appointed Zhang Xiu as Governor of Jingzhao; for this they recalled Xiu and gave Guangyuan his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore pretended to send his son east to see An Lushan, but Lushan had already appointed Zhang Xiu governor of Jingzhao; Xiu was recalled for this, and Guangyuan was given his former post.

sentences.zh: 俄而同羅背賊，以廄馬二千出奔，賊將孫孝哲、安神威招之不得，神威憂死，官吏驚走，獄囚皆逸。

translations.literal: Soon the Tongluo turned against the rebels, with two thousand stable horses fled out; rebel generals Sun Xiaozhe and An Shenwei could not win them; Shenwei died of grief; officials fled in alarm; prison inmates all escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Tongluo turned against the rebels and fled with two thousand stable horses. The rebel generals Sun Xiaozhe and An Shenwei could not win them over; Shenwei died of grief; officials fled in alarm, and all the prisoners escaped.

sentences.zh: 光遠以為賊且走，命人守神威、孝哲等第，斬曳落河二人。

translations.literal: Guangyuan thought the rebels were about to flee, ordered men to guard the residences of Shenwei, Xiaozhe, and the rest, beheaded two Tiele guards.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan thought the rebels were about to flee; he had men guard the residences of Shenwei, Xiaozhe, and the others, and beheaded two Tiele guards.

sentences.zh: 孝哲馳白祿山，光遠懼，與長安令蘇震出開遠門，使人奔呼曰：「尹巡門！」

translations.literal: Xiaozhe galloped to report to Lushan; Guangyuan was afraid; with Chang'an magistrate Su Zhen he went out Kaiyuan Gate, had men run shouting: "The Governor inspects the gate!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhe galloped to report to Lushan. Guangyuan was afraid; he went with Chang'an magistrate Su Zhen out through Kaiyuan Gate and had men run ahead shouting, "The governor is inspecting the gate!"

sentences.zh: 門兵具器仗迎謁，至，皆斬之，募得百餘人，遂趨靈武。

translations.literal: Gate soldiers equipped weapons to receive and attend; when they arrived, all were beheaded; he recruited more than a hundred men, then hastened toward Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: The gate soldiers came out with weapons to receive him; when they arrived, he beheaded them all, recruited more than a hundred men, and hastened toward Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 肅宗嘉之，擢拜御史大夫，復為京兆尹，遣到渭北募僑民。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong praised this, promoted to Censor-in-Chief, again made Governor of Jingzhao, sent to north of the Wei to recruit displaced people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong praised this, promoted him to censor-in-chief, again made him governor of Jingzhao, and sent him north of the Wei to recruit displaced people.

sentences.zh: 會賊黨剽涇陽，休祠房，椎牛呼飲。

translations.literal: It happened rebel bands raided Jingyang; they rested in a shrine building, slaughtered oxen and shouted while drinking.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel bands raided Jingyang, they rested in a shrine building, slaughtered oxen, and feasted with loud shouting.

sentences.zh: 光遠刺知之，率兵夜趨其所，使百騎彀滿狙其前，命驍士合噪。

translations.literal: Guangyuan learned through spies, led troops by night toward their place, made a hundred horsemen with bows full to ambush before them, ordered fierce soldiers to shout together.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan learned of it through spies, led troops by night toward their camp, stationed a hundred horsemen with drawn bows to ambush them in front, and ordered his fiercest soldiers to shout in unison.

sentences.zh: 賊醉，不能師，斬其徒二千，得馬千噭，俘一酋長以獻。

translations.literal: The rebels were drunk, could not form ranks, beheaded two thousand of their followers, obtained a thousand neighing horses, captured one chieftain to present.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were drunk and could not form ranks; he beheaded two thousand of their followers, took a thousand neighing horses, and presented one chieftain as prisoner.

sentences.zh: 自是，賊常避其鋒。

translations.literal: From this, rebels regularly avoided his sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the rebels regularly avoided his sharp edge.

sentences.zh: 扈帝還，改禮部尚書、鄴國公，封實戶三百。

translations.literal: Escorting the Emperor back, changed to Minister of Rites, Duke of Ye, enfeoffed three hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the emperor back, he was made minister of rites and Duke of Ye, with three hundred taxable households as his fief.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，繇汴州刺史代蕭華為魏州節度使。

translations.literal: First year of Qianyuan, from Governor of Bianzhou replaced Xiao Hua as Military Governor of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan, he went from governor of Bianzhou to replace Xiao Hua as military governor of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，郭子儀與賊戰汲郡，光遠裁率汴師千人援之，不甚力。

translations.literal: At first, when Guo Ziyi fought rebels at Ji Commandery, Guangyuan had only led a thousand Bian troops to aid him, not very strenuously.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Guo Ziyi fought the rebels at Ji Commandery, Guangyuan had led only a thousand Bian troops to his aid and had not exerted himself greatly.

sentences.zh: 及守魏，使將軍李處拒賊，子儀不救，戰不勝，奔還，賊因傅城下詭呼曰：「處召我而不出，何也？」

translations.literal: When defending Wei, he sent General Li Chu to resist rebels; Ziyi did not rescue; battle not victorious, fled back; rebels thereupon spread below the walls a false call: "Chu summoned us but will not come out—why?"
translations.idiomatic: When he was defending Wei, he sent the general Li Chu to resist the rebels; Ziyi did not rescue him; the battle was lost and Chu fled back. The rebels then spread a false call below the walls: "Chu summoned us and will not come out—why?"

sentences.zh: 光遠信之，斬處。

translations.literal: Guangyuan believed it and beheaded Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan believed it and beheaded Chu.

sentences.zh: 處善戰，眾倚以為重，及死，人益危。

translations.literal: Chu was skilled in battle; the masses relied on him as weighty; when he died, men grew still more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Chu was skilled in battle and the troops relied on him as their mainstay; when he died, the men grew still more fearful.

sentences.zh: 魏城經袁知泰、能元皓等完築，牢甚，光遠不能守，夜潰圍出，奔京師。

translations.literal: The city of Wei had been fully built by Yuan Zhitai, Neng Yuanhao, and others; very secure; Guangyuan could not hold it, by night broke the encirclement and went out, fled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The city of Wei had been fully fortified by Yuan Zhitai, Neng Yuanhao, and others and was very strong; Guangyuan could not hold it, broke the siege by night and fled out, and ran to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝赦其罪，拜太子少保。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned his offense, appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned his offense and appointed him grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 會襄州將康楚元、張嘉延反，陷荊、襄諸州，因拜持節荊、襄招討，充山南東道兵馬都使。

translations.literal: It happened Xiangzhou generals Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan rebelled, seized Jing and Xiang prefectures; he was therefore appointed Commissioner with credentials for Jing-Xiang pacification, concurrent overall commander of Shannan East Route forces.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiangzhou generals Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan rebelled and seized the Jing and Xiang prefectures, he was appointed commissioner with credentials for Jing-Xiang pacification and overall commander of Shannan East Route forces.

sentences.zh: 又徙鳳翔尹。

translations.literal: Again transferred to Governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 先是，岐、隴賊郭愔等掠州縣，峙五堡，光遠至，遣官喻降之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qishan and Longyou bandits Guo Yin and others plundered prefectures and counties, held five fortified camps; when Guangyuan arrived, he sent officials to persuade them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Qishan and Longyou bandits Guo Yin and others had plundered prefectures and counties and held five fortified camps; when Guangyuan arrived, he sent officials to persuade them to surrender.

sentences.zh: 既而沈飲不親事，愔等陰約党項及奴剌、突厥，敗韋倫於秦、隴，殺監軍使。

translations.literal: Afterward he sank into drink and did not attend to affairs; Yin and the rest secretly allied with the Tangut and the Nulu and Turks, defeated Wei Lun in Qin and Long, killed the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sank into drink and neglected affairs; Yin and the rest secretly allied with the Tangut, Nulu, and Turks, defeated Wei Lun in Qin and Long, and killed the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 帝怒光遠無狀，召還。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry that Guangyuan had behaved without restraint and summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry that Guangyuan had behaved without restraint and summoned him back.

sentences.zh: 復使節度劍南。

translations.literal: Again sent to command Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent to command Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 會段子璋反東川，李奐敗走成都，光遠進討平之。

translations.literal: It happened Duan Zizhang rebelled in Dongchuan; Li Huan was defeated and fled to Chengdu; Guangyuan advanced, attacked, and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Zizhang rebelled in Dongchuan and Li Huan was defeated and fled to Chengdu, Guangyuan advanced, attacked, and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 然不能禁士卒剽掠士女，至斷腕取金者，夷殺數千人。

translations.literal: Yet he could not restrain soldiers from plundering gentlemen and women, even to cutting wrists to take gold; he barbarously killed several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not restrain his soldiers from plundering men and women—even cutting off wrists to take gold—and he barbarously killed several thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝詔監軍按其罪，以憂卒。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the army supervisor to investigate his crimes; he died of anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the army supervisor to investigate his crimes; he died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 鄧景山，曹州人。

translations.literal: Deng Jingshan, a man of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jingshan was a native of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 本以文吏進，累至監察御史。

translations.literal: Originally entered through the civil clerk track, rose repeatedly to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally entered through the civil-service track and rose to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 至德初，擢拜青齊節度使，徙淮南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, promoted as Military Governor of Qing and Qi, transferred to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhide era he was promoted to military governor of Qing and Qi, then transferred to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 為政簡肅。

translations.literal: His government was simple and austere.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was simple and austere.

sentences.zh: 有鼉集城門，鄧珽語景山曰：「鼉介物也。

translations.literal: A crocodile gathered at the city gate; Deng Ting said to Jingshan: "The crocodile is a scaled creature.
translations.idiomatic: A crocodile gathered at the city gate. Deng Ting said to Jingshan, "The crocodile is a scaled creature.

sentences.zh: 失所次，金不從革之象。

translations.literal: Out of its proper place—an image of metal not following transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Out of its proper place—an omen of metal not yielding to change.

sentences.zh: 其有兵乎？」

translations.literal: Will there be warfare?"
translations.idiomatic: Does this portend warfare?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，宋州刺史劉殿反。

translations.literal: Before long, Songzhou Prefect Liu Dian rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Songzhou prefect Liu Zhan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 初，展有異志，淮西節度使王仲昇表其狀，詔遷揚州長史兼江淮都統，密詔景山執送京師。

translations.literal: At first Zhan had a different intent; Huainan West Military Governor Wang Zhongsheng memorialized his conduct; edict moved him to Yangzhou Chief Administrator concurrent Commander of Jiang-Huai, secret edict to Jingshan to arrest and send to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Zhan had harbored a different intent; Huainan West military governor Wang Zhongsheng memorialized his conduct; the emperor ordered him moved to Yangzhou chief administrator and concurrent commander of Jiang-Huai, with a secret edict to Jingshan to arrest him and send him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 展知之，擁兵二萬度淮。

translations.literal: Zhan learned of it, led twenty thousand troops across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan learned of it and led twenty thousand troops across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 景山逆擊不勝，奔壽州，因引平盧節度副使田神功討展。

translations.literal: Jingshan met him in attack and was not victorious, fled to Shouzhou, then brought in Pinglu Deputy Military Governor Tian Shenggong to attack Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan met him in attack and was defeated; he fled to Shouzhou and then brought in Pinglu deputy military governor Tian Shenggong to attack Zhan.

sentences.zh: 神功兵至揚州，大掠居人，發冢墓，大食、波斯賈胡死者數千人。

translations.literal: When Shenggong's army reached Yangzhou, they greatly plundered inhabitants, opened graves; Sogdian and Persian merchant dead numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenggong's army reached Yangzhou, they greatly plundered the inhabitants and opened graves; several thousand Sogdian and Persian merchants were among the dead.

sentences.zh: 展叛凡三月平，追景山入朝，拜尚書左丞，以崔圓代之。

translations.literal: Zhan's rebellion was pacified in about three months; Jingshan was recalled to court, appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Cui Yuan replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's rebellion was pacified in about three months; Jingshan was recalled to court, appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and Cui Yuan replaced him.

sentences.zh: 王思禮在太原，儲廥贏衍，請輸半以實京師。

translations.literal: Wang Sili was at Taiyuan; granaries full and overflowing; he requested shipping half to fill the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sili was at Taiyuan with granaries full and overflowing; he requested shipping half the stores to fill the capital.

sentences.zh: 會卒，管崇嗣代之，政弛不治，數月，為下盜費略盡。

translations.literal: He soon died; Guan Chongsi replaced him; government grew slack and was not put in order; within months what the lower ranks stole and wasted was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died; Guan Chongsi replaced him; government grew slack and was not put in order; within months theft and waste by the lower ranks had nearly exhausted everything.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，即以景山為太原尹，封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he at once made Jingshan Governor of Taiyuan and enfeoffed him Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he at once made Jingshan governor of Taiyuan and enfeoffed him as Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 至則振核紀綱，檢覆幹隱，眾大懼。

translations.literal: On arrival he shook up discipline and regulations, investigated concealed abuses; the masses were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he shook up discipline and regulations and investigated concealed abuses; the masses were greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 而景山清約，子弟饌不過草具，用器止烏漆，待上賓惟豚、魚而已，取倉粟紅腐者食之，兼給麾下，麾下怨訕。

translations.literal: Yet Jingshan was frugal and abstemious; sons and brothers' meals were no more than humble fare; vessels only black lacquer; for honored guests only pork and fish; he took red rotten grain from the granary to eat and also gave to his subordinates—the subordinates grumbled in ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jingshan was frugal and abstemious: his sons and brothers' meals were no more than humble fare, his vessels were only black lacquer, and for honored guests he served only pork and fish. He took red rotten grain from the granary to eat and also gave it to his subordinates, who grumbled in ridicule.

sentences.zh: 左右白景山，景山曰：「此不食，留將安用邪？」

translations.literal: Attendants informed Jingshan; Jingshan said: "If we won't eat this, what will we keep it for?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants informed Jingshan; Jingshan said, "If we won't eat this, what will we keep it for?"

sentences.zh: 因慢罵，士皆羞忿。

translations.literal: He then reviled them with contempt, and the soldiers were all ashamed and furious.
translations.idiomatic: He then reviled them with contempt, and the soldiers were all ashamed and furious.

sentences.zh: 有裨校抵死，諸將請贖，不許；

translations.literal: A staff officer was guilty of a capital offense; the generals asked to redeem him—not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: A staff officer was guilty of a capital offense; the generals asked to redeem him—not permitted;

sentences.zh: 其弟請代，不許；

translations.literal: his younger brother asked to take his place—not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother asked to take his place—not permitted;

sentences.zh: 請納一馬贖，景山乃許減死。

translations.literal: they asked to offer one horse in ransom; only then did Jingshan permit commutation from death.
translations.idiomatic: they asked to offer one horse in ransom; only then did Jingshan permit commutation from death.

sentences.zh: 眾怒曰：「吾屬命才一馬直乎？」

translations.literal: The crowd raged, saying: "Are our lives worth only one horse?"
translations.idiomatic: The crowd raged, saying, "Are our lives worth only one horse?"

sentences.zh: 景山護失，叱遣之。

translations.literal: Jingshan, protective of his error, shouted and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan, protective of his error, shouted and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 少將黃抱節因眾怒作亂，景山遇害，時寶應元年也。

translations.literal: The junior general Huang Baojie, because of the crowd's anger, made a revolt; Jingshan met disaster—it was the first year of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: The junior general Huang Baojie stirred up the crowd's anger and made a revolt; Jingshan met his death—it was the first year of Baoying.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以其統馭失方，不復究驗，遣使喻撫其軍，軍中請辛雲京為節度，詔可。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong, because he had lost control, did not pursue investigation further, sent envoys to pacify the army; the army requested Xin Yunjing as military governor; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong, because Jingshan had lost control, did not pursue the matter further; he sent envoys to pacify the army, and the army requested Xin Yunjing as military governor—the edict approved.

sentences.zh: 景山與劉晏善，其後家寒窶，晏屢經紀之，嫁其孤女。

translations.literal: Jingshan was on good terms with Liu Yan; afterward his family was poor and needy; Yan repeatedly managed affairs for him and married off his orphaned daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan was friendly with Liu Yan; afterward his family was poor and needy, and Yan repeatedly managed affairs for him and married off his orphaned daughter.

sentences.zh: 謚曰敬。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jing.

sentences.zh: 崔瓘，博陵人，以士行修謹聞。

translations.literal: Cui Guan, a man of Boling, was known for cultivated conduct and careful propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guan, a man of Boling, was known for cultivated conduct and careful propriety.

sentences.zh: 累官至澧州刺史，不為煩苛，人便安之，流亡還歸，居二年，增戶數萬。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Prefect of Li; he was not troublesome or severe; people found him convenient and settled; exiles returned; in two years households increased by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through offices to prefect of Li; he was not troublesome or severe; people found him convenient and settled; exiles returned; in two years households increased by tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 詔特進五階，以寵異政。

translations.literal: An edict specially advanced him five steps in rank to reward distinctive administration.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially advanced him five steps in rank to reward his distinctive administration.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，遷湖南觀察使，時將吏習寬弛，不奉法，瓘稍以禮法繩裁之，下多怨。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he was transferred to Hunan Observation Commissioner; at the time generals and clerks were accustomed to laxness and did not obey law; Guan gradually restrained them with ritual and law; those below bore much resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era he was transferred to Hunan observation commissioner; at the time generals and clerks were accustomed to laxness and did not obey the law; Guan gradually restrained them with ritual and law, and those below bore much resentment.

sentences.zh: 別將臧玠、判官達奚覯忿爭，覯曰：「今幸無事。」

translations.literal: Deputy commander Zang Jie and judicial officer Dazi Gun quarreled in anger; Gun said: "We are fortunate to have no trouble now."
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commander Zang Jie and the judicial officer Daxi Gou quarreled in anger; Gou said, "We are fortunate to have no trouble now."

sentences.zh: 玠曰：「欲有事邪？」

translations.literal: Jie said: "Do you want there to be trouble?"
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "Do you want there to be trouble?"

sentences.zh: 拂衣去，是夜以兵殺覯。

translations.literal: He flung his robe and left; that night he killed Gun with troops.
translations.idiomatic: He flung his robe and left; that night he killed Gou with troops.

sentences.zh: 瓘聞難，惶懼走，遇害，帝悼惜之。

translations.literal: Guan heard of the calamity, fled in panic, met his death; the Emperor mourned and prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan heard of the calamity, fled in panic, and met his death; the emperor mourned and prized him.

sentences.zh: 魏少遊，字少遊，邢州鉅鹿人，以吏幹稱。

translations.literal: Wei Shaoyou, styled Shaoyou, a man of Julu in Xingzhou, was famed for competence as an administrative officer.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shaoyou, styled Shaoyou, was a man of Julu in Xingzhou, famed for competence as an administrative officer.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，累遷朔方水陸轉運副使。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he rose repeatedly to Deputy Commissioner for Shuo-fang Water and Land Transport.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he rose repeatedly to deputy commissioner for Shuo-fang water and land transport.

sentences.zh: 肅宗幸靈武，杜鴻漸等奉迎，而留少遊繕治宮室。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reached Lingwu, Du Hongjian and others went to welcome him, while Shaoyou was left to repair the palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong reached Lingwu, Du Hongjian and others went to welcome him, while Shaoyou was left to repair the palaces.

sentences.zh: 少遊大為殿宇幄帟，皆象宮闕，諸王、公主悉有次舍，供擬窮水陸。

translations.literal: Shaoyou greatly built halls and curtains patterned after the palace precincts; all princes and princesses had lodging in turn; provisions exhausted over land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou greatly built halls and curtains patterned after the palace precincts; all the princes and princesses had their lodging in turn; provisions were exhausted over land and water.

sentences.zh: 又有千餘騎，鎧幟光鮮，振旅以入。

translations.literal: There were also more than a thousand riders, armor and banners bright and fresh, entering in martial array.
translations.idiomatic: There were also more than a thousand riders, armor and banners bright and fresh, entering in martial array.

sentences.zh: 帝見宮殿，不悅曰：「我至此欲就大事，安用是為？」

translations.literal: The Emperor saw the palaces and was displeased, saying: "I came here to accomplish the great affair—what need is there for this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the palaces and was displeased, saying, "I came here to accomplish the great affair—what need is there for this?"

sentences.zh: 稍命去之。

translations.literal: He then gradually ordered it removed.
translations.idiomatic: He then gradually ordered it removed.

sentences.zh: 除左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Department Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left department vice director.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，封鉅鹿縣侯，遷陜州刺史。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Julu and transferred to Governor of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were pacified, he was enfeoffed as marquis of Julu and transferred to governor of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 王師潰於鄴，河、洛震駭，少遊鎮守自若。

translations.literal: Imperial armies were routed at Ye; the Yellow and Luo rivers were shaken with terror; Shaoyou held his post calmly as before.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial armies were routed at Ye, the Yellow and Luo regions were shaken with terror; Shaoyou held his post calmly as before.

sentences.zh: 擢京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 李輔國以其不附己，改衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo, because he did not attach himself to him, changed him to Chamberlain for the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo, because he did not attach himself to him, changed him to chamberlain for the guard.

sentences.zh: 會率群臣馬助軍，少遊與漢中王瑀持異，帝怒，貶渠州長史。

translations.literal: At an assembly where the court led horses to aid the armies, Shaoyou differed with Prince of Hanzhong Wang Yu; the Emperor was angry and demoted him to Chief Administrator of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At an assembly where the court led horses to aid the armies, Shaoyou differed with Prince of Hanzhong Wang Yu; the emperor was angry and demoted him to chief administrator of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 復為京兆尹，始請：「中書門下省五品、尚書省四品、諸司正員三品、諸王、駙馬期以上親及婿若甥，不得任京兆官。」

translations.literal: Again made Governor of Jingzhao, he first requested: "Fifth rank of Secretariat-Chancellery, fourth rank of Department of State Affairs, regular third rank in various bureaus, princes, and sons-in-law of the emperor at first rank and above and their sons-in-law or nephews may not hold Jingzhao office."
translations.idiomatic: Again made governor of Jingzhao, he first requested: "Fifth rank of the Secretariat-Chancellery, fourth rank of the Department of State Affairs, regular third rank in the various bureaus, princes, and sons-in-law of the emperor at first rank and above and their sons-in-law or nephews may not hold Jingzhao office."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 大歷二年，為江西觀察使，進刑部尚書，改封趙國公。

translations.literal: Second year of Dali, he was Jiangxi Observation Commissioner, promoted to Minister of Justice, enfeoffment changed to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dali he was Jiangxi observation commissioner, promoted to minister of justice, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 六年卒，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died; he was posthumously made grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 少遊四為京兆，雖無赫赫名，然善任人，緣飾規檢，有足稱者。

translations.literal: Shaoyou served four terms as Jingzhao; though he had no towering reputation, yet he was good at employing men and adorning regulations and inspections, and had points worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou served four terms as Jingzhao governor; though he had no towering reputation, he was good at employing men and adorning regulations and inspections, and had points worth praising.

sentences.zh: 衞伯玉，史失其何所人。

translations.literal: Wei Boyu. The histories lose where he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Boyu — the histories do not record his birthplace.

sentences.zh: 少習武技，為有力。

translations.literal: In youth he studied martial arts and was powerful.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied martial arts and was powerful.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，從安西府，積勞至員外諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he served in the Anxi headquarters and through accumulated merit rose to extrabureau general of the various guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he served in the Anxi headquarters and through accumulated merit rose to extrabureau general of the various guards.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，慨然願立功，乃歸長安，領神策兵馬使，出鎮陜州行營。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, Boyu ardently wished to achieve merit; he returned to Chang'an, took command as Shence army commander, and went out to garrison the Shanzhou campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne, Boyu ardently wished to achieve merit. He returned to Chang'an, took command as Shence army commander, and went out to garrison the Shanzhou campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，賊將李歸仁以騎五千入寇，伯玉與戰強子阪，破之，獲馬六百匹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan, rebel general Li Guiren invaded with five thousand cavalry; Boyu fought him at Qiangzi Slope, defeated him, and seized six hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyuan, rebel general Li Guiren invaded with five thousand cavalry. Boyu fought him at Qiangzi Slope, defeated him, and seized six hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 遷羽林大將軍，徙四鎮、北庭行營節度使，俄為神策軍節度。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand general of the Yulin Guard, reassigned as military commissioner of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign headquarters, and soon became military commissioner of the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand general of the Yulin Guard, reassigned as military commissioner of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign headquarters, and soon became military commissioner of the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 史思明遣子朝義夜襲陜，將動京師，伯玉迎擊，破之於永寧。

translations.literal: Shi Siming sent his son Chaoyi to raid Shan by night, intending to shake the capital; Boyu met the attack and defeated him at Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming sent his son Chaoyi to raid Shan by night, intending to shake the capital. Boyu met the attack and defeated him at Yongning.

sentences.zh: 加特進，封河東郡公。

translations.literal: He was given the superlative precedence rank and enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the superlative precedence rank and enfeoffed as duke of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，代宗幸陜，以伯玉有幹略，可方面大事，乃拜荊南節度使，進封城陽郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, when Daizong visited Shan, considering Boyu had capacity and resolve fit for a major regional command, he was appointed military commissioner of Jingnan and advanced to prince of Chengyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangde, when Daizong visited Shan, considering Boyu had capacity and resolve fit for a major regional command, he was appointed military commissioner of Jingnan and advanced to prince of Chengyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，以母憂當代，諷將吏留己，復詔節度荊南，議者醜其留。

translations.literal: Early in the Dali era, when he should have been replaced on account of mourning for his mother, he incited officers and clerks to keep him in office; an edict again appointed him military commissioner of Jingnan — those who discussed it despised his retention.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali era, when he should have been replaced on account of mourning for his mother, he incited officers and clerks to keep him in office. An edict again appointed him military commissioner of Jingnan, and those who discussed it despised his retention.

sentences.zh: 十一年，歸京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 李澄，遼東襄平人，隋蒲山公寬之遠胄。

translations.literal: Li Cheng was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, a distant descendant of Duke Kuan of Pushan in the Sui dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, a distant descendant of Duke Kuan of Pushan in the Sui dynasty.

sentences.zh: 以勇剽隸江淮都統李亙府為偏將。

translations.literal: For his boldness and raiding skill he was attached to the headquarters of Li Gen, overall commander of the Jianghuai region, as a deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: For his boldness and raiding skill he was attached to the headquarters of Li Gen, overall commander of the Jianghuai region, as a deputy general.

sentences.zh: 又從永平節度李勉軍，勉帥汴，表澄滑州刺史。

translations.literal: He later followed the Yongping military commissioner Li Mian's army; when Mian took Bian as headquarters, he memorialized for Cheng to be prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Yongping military commissioner Li Mian's army. When Mian took Bian as headquarters, he memorialized for Cheng to be prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 李希烈陷汴，勉走，澄以城降賊，希烈以為尚書令，節度永平軍。

translations.literal: Li Xilie took Bian; Mian fled; Cheng surrendered the city to the rebels, and Xilie made him chancellor and military commissioner of Yongping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie took Bian. Mian fled, and Cheng surrendered the city to the rebels. Xilie made him chancellor and military commissioner of Yongping Army.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，澄遣盧融間道奉表詣行在。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, Cheng sent Lu Rong by a hidden route bearing a memorial to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan, Cheng sent Lu Rong by a hidden route bearing a memorial to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，署帛詔內蜜丸，授澄刑部尚書、汴滑節度使，澄未即宣，乃行勒訓士馬。

translations.literal: Dezong commended this, placed the silk edict within a wax pellet, and appointed Cheng minister of justice and military commissioner of Bian and Hua; Cheng did not announce it at once, but went out drilling and training troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong commended this, placed the silk edict within a wax pellet, and appointed Cheng minister of justice and military commissioner of Bian and Hua. Cheng did not announce it at once, but went out drilling and training troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 希烈疑，以養子六百戍之。

translations.literal: Xilie grew suspicious and posted six hundred adopted sons as garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie grew suspicious and posted six hundred adopted sons as garrison there.

sentences.zh: 賊急攻寧陵，邀澄至石柱，澄密令焚營為驚遁者，養子輩果乘以剽掠，澄盡斬之，以告，希烈不能詰。

translations.literal: The rebels pressed hard against Ningling and summoned Cheng to Shizhu; Cheng secretly ordered the camp burned as though in panicked flight; the adopted sons indeed took advantage to loot; Cheng had them all beheaded and reported it, and Xilie could not pursue the matter further.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed hard against Ningling and summoned Cheng to Shizhu. Cheng secretly ordered the camp burned as though in panicked flight. The adopted sons indeed took advantage to loot, and Cheng had them all beheaded and reported it. Xilie could not pursue the matter further.

sentences.zh: 賊遣將翟崇暉率精兵寇陳州，未還，汴軍寡，澄度不能制己，又中官薛盈珍持節至，封澄武威郡王，賜實封，乃燔賊旗節自歸。

translations.literal: The rebels sent general Zhai Chonghui with elite troops to raid Chenzhou; before he returned, Bian had few troops; Cheng judged that Xilie could no longer control him; moreover the palace eunuch Xue Yingzhen arrived bearing credentials, enfeoffing Cheng as prince of Wuwei commandery and granting a permanent fief; Cheng thereupon burned the rebel banners and credentials and returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent general Zhai Chonghui with elite troops to raid Chenzhou. Before he returned, Bian had few troops, and Cheng judged that Xilie could no longer control him. Moreover the palace eunuch Xue Yingzhen arrived bearing credentials, enfeoffing Cheng as prince of Wuwei commandery and granting a permanent fief. Cheng thereupon burned the rebel banners and credentials and returned to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 希烈既失澄，而崇暉復敗，由是奔汝南。

translations.literal: Xilie having lost Cheng, and Chonghui again defeated, on this account fled to Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie having lost Cheng, and Chonghui again defeated, on this account fled to Runan.

sentences.zh: 澄引兵將取汴，屯其北門不敢進，及劉洽師屯東門，賊將田懷珍納之。

translations.literal: Cheng led troops intending to take Bian, camped at its north gate and dared not advance; when Liu He's army camped at the east gate, rebel general Tian Huaizhen surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng led troops intending to take Bian, camped at its north gate and dared not advance; when Liu Qia's army camped at the east gate, the rebel general Tian Huaizhen surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 比澄入，洽已保子城矣。

translations.literal: By the time Cheng entered, He had already held the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Cheng entered, He had already held the inner city.

sentences.zh: 澄乃舍浚儀，兩軍士日爭忿，未能安。

translations.literal: Cheng then abandoned Junyi; the soldiers of the two armies quarreled daily in resentment and could not settle.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng then abandoned Junyi; the soldiers of the two armies quarreled daily in resentment and could not settle down.

sentences.zh: 會鄭州賊將孫液送款於澄，澄遣子清馳赴。

translations.literal: It happened Zhengzhou rebel general Sun Ye sent terms to Cheng; Cheng sent his son Qing galloping to respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengzhou rebel general Sun Ye sent terms to Cheng, Cheng sent his son Qing galloping to respond.

sentences.zh: 先此，河陽李芃使偏將雍希顥攻鄭，數殘剽，液拒之。

translations.literal: Before this, Heyang's Li Peng had sent his deputy Yong Xixian to attack Zheng, repeatedly cruelly raiding; Ye resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Li Peng of Heyang had sent his deputy Yong Xixian to attack Zheng, repeatedly raiding with cruelty; Ye resisted him.

sentences.zh: 及納清，希顥大怒，急攻鄭。

translations.literal: When Qing was received, Xixian was greatly angered and urgently attacked Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing was received, Xixian was greatly angered and urgently attacked Zheng.

sentences.zh: 清助守，殺河陽兵數千，希顥焚陽武去，澄遂如鄭。

translations.literal: Qing helped defend; killed several thousand Heyang troops; Xixian burned Yangwu and left; Cheng then went to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qing helped defend, killed several thousand Heyang troops; Xixian burned Yangwu and left; Cheng then went to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 詔授清檢校太子賓客，易名克寧。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Qing Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent and changed his name to Kening.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Qing acting guest of the heir apparent and changed his name to Kening.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，遷澄檢校尚書左僕射、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, Cheng was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Military Governor of Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era, Cheng was made acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and military governor of the Yicheng army.

sentences.zh: 二年卒，年五十四，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, age fifty-four; posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died at the age of fifty-four and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 澄始封隴西公，後乃進王爵，每上章，必疊署二封，士大夫笑其野。

translations.literal: Cheng was first enfeoffed Duke of Longxi, later advanced to princely rank; whenever he submitted a memorial he would stack two signatures; scholar-officials laughed at his rusticity.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was first enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi and later advanced to princely rank; whenever he submitted a memorial he would sign it twice, and the scholar-officials laughed at his rustic manners.

sentences.zh: 澄之喪，克寧不發，閱旬日，欲自領事，其行軍司馬馬鉉不許，克寧殺之，墨绖，加卒嬰城，將為亂。

translations.literal: At Cheng's mourning, Kening did not begin the funeral; after ten days he wished to take command himself; his campaigning deputy Ma Xuan did not permit it; Kening killed him, wore ink mourning, added troops to man the walls, and was about to make a revolt.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died, Kening did not begin the funeral rites; after ten days he wished to take command himself, but his campaigning deputy Ma Xuan would not permit it, so Kening killed him, wore ink mourning, reinforced the walls with troops, and was about to rebel.

sentences.zh: 劉洽以兵屯境上，遣使諭止，遂自戢，然道閉者半月。

translations.literal: Liu He stationed troops on the border, sent envoys to instruct and stop him; he then restrained himself, yet the roads were closed for half a month.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia stationed troops on the border and sent envoys to instruct him to stop; Kening then restrained himself, yet the roads remained closed for half a month.

sentences.zh: 詔以賈耽代鎮，克寧乃護喪歸，悉索府中財夜出，軍士從剽之殆盡，澄柩至京，猶賜克寧莊一區、錢千緡、粟麥數千石雲。

translations.literal: An edict made Jia Dan replace him in command; Kening then escorted the coffin back, searched out all the wealth in the headquarters by night and took it out; soldiers followed in plundering until nearly exhausted; when Cheng's coffin reached the capital, Kening was still granted one estate, a thousand strings of cash, and several thousand piculs of grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Jia Dan to replace him in command; Kening then escorted the coffin home, searched out all the headquarters wealth by night and carried it away, and the soldiers followed in plundering until nearly nothing remained. When Cheng's coffin reached the capital, Kening was still granted an estate, a thousand strings of cash, and several thousand piculs of grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 韓全義，家素寒，史失其先世。

translations.literal: Han Quanyi, his family always poor; the histories have lost his forebears.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanyi came from a family that had always been poor, and the histories have lost record of his forebears.

sentences.zh: 興卒伍，以巧佞事宦者竇文場，擢累長武城使，進拜夏綏銀宥節度使，詔以長武兵赴之。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks of soldiers, by crafty flattery served the eunuch Dou Wenchang, was promoted repeatedly to Changwu Fort commander, advanced to Military Governor of Xia-Sui-Yin-You, with an edict that Changwu troops go to join him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks of soldiers and, through crafty flattery, served the eunuch Dou Wenchang; he was promoted repeatedly to Changwu Fort commander and then to military governor of Xia-Sui-Yin-You, with an edict that Changwu troops go to join him.

sentences.zh: 全義素懦貪，無紀律，為下靳狎。

translations.literal: Quanyi was by nature cowardly and greedy, without discipline, and was treated familiarly and slightingly by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi was by nature cowardly and greedy, without discipline, and his subordinates treated him familiarly and slightingly.

sentences.zh: 詔未下，軍中遍知之，謀曰：「夏州沙磧，無樹蓺生業，不可往。」

translations.literal: Before the edict was issued, the whole army knew it and plotted, saying: "Xiazhou is sandy desert, without trees or crops for livelihood—we cannot go."
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict was issued, the whole army already knew of it and plotted among themselves, saying, "Xiazhou is sandy desert, without trees or crops for a livelihood—we cannot go there."

sentences.zh: 是夜，噪而亂，全義縋以逸，殺其親將王棲巖、趙虔曜等，軍虞候高崇文誅亂首，眾乃定，全義得赴屯。

translations.literal: That night they clamored and rioted; Quanyi lowered himself by rope and escaped; they killed his close generals Wang Qiyan, Zhao Qianyao, and others; army adjutant Gao Chongwen executed the ringleaders of the disorder, and the masses then settled; Quanyi was able to go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: That night they clamored and rioted; Quanyi lowered himself by rope and escaped; they killed his close generals Wang Qiyan, Zhao Qianyao, and others; the army adjutant Gao Chongwen executed the ringleaders, and the troops then settled down; Quanyi was able to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠以蔡拒命，詔合十七鎮兵討之。

translations.literal: Wu Shaocheng defied orders with Cai; an edict combined troops from seventeen circuits to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Shaocheng defied orders at Cai, an edict combined troops from seventeen circuits to attack him.

sentences.zh: 時軍無帥統，惟以奄豎監之，遂敗於小溵。

translations.literal: At the time the army had no commander-in-chief; only eunuchs supervised it; they were therefore defeated at Xiaoshui.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the army had no commander-in-chief and was supervised only by eunuchs; they were therefore defeated at Xiaoshui.

sentences.zh: 德宗以文場素為全義地，因用為淮西行營招討使，以陳許節度使上官涚副之，諸鎮兵皆屬。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong, because Wenchang had always been Quanyi's patron, therefore used him as Huainan West Pacification Commissioner, with Chenxu Military Governor Shangguan Shui as deputy; troops from all circuits were subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, because Wenchang had always been Quanyi's patron, appointed him pacification commissioner for the Huainan West campaign, with Chenxu military governor Shangguan Shui as his deputy; troops from all the circuits were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 全義無它方略，號令悉稟監軍，每議攻戰，宦豎十數紛爭帳中，小人好自異，互詆訾不能決。

translations.literal: Quanyi had no other strategy; orders all submitted to the army supervisors; whenever attack and battle were discussed, a dozen eunuchs quarreled in the tent; petty men liked to differ from one another and mutually slandered until no decision could be made.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi had no strategy of his own; all orders were submitted to the army supervisors. Whenever attack and battle were discussed, a dozen eunuchs quarreled in the tent; petty men liked to differ from one another and mutually slandered until no decision could be reached.

sentences.zh: 賊知之，數請戰。

translations.literal: The rebels knew this and repeatedly requested battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels knew this and repeatedly offered battle.

sentences.zh: 遇賊廣利城，方暑，地沮洳，士皆病癘，全義未嘗存之。

translations.literal: They met the rebels at Guangli City; it was midsummer; the ground was damp and marshy; the soldiers all fell ill with miasma; Quanyi had never looked after them.
translations.idiomatic: They met the rebels at Guangli City in midsummer on damp, marshy ground; the soldiers all fell ill with miasma, and Quanyi had never looked after them.

sentences.zh: 既戰，師皆潰，退保五樓，賊移屯逼之，乃與監軍賈英秀等保溵水，不能固，又入屯陳州。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, the armies all collapsed; they retreated to hold Wulou; the rebels moved camp to press them; then with army supervisor Jia Yingxiu and others they held the Wen River but could not secure it, and again entered camp at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once battle was joined, the armies collapsed; they retreated to hold Wulou; the rebels moved camp to press them; then with army supervisor Jia Yingxiu and others they tried to hold the Wen River but could not secure it and withdrew again to camp at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，唯陳許將孟元陽、神策將蘇光榮守溵水，全義誘潞、滑州數大將殺之，然卒不振。

translations.literal: At this time only Chenxu general Meng Yuanyang and Shence general Su Guangrong held the Wen River; Quanyi enticed several great generals of Lu and Hua prefectures and killed them, yet in the end could not recover.
translations.idiomatic: At this time only Chenxu general Meng Yuanyang and Shence general Su Guangrong held the Wen River; Quanyi enticed and killed several great generals of Lu and Hua prefectures, yet in the end could not recover.

sentences.zh: 宦人共掩其敗，帝不知。

translations.literal: The eunuchs together concealed his defeat; the Emperor did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs together concealed his defeat, and the emperor did not know.

sentences.zh: 少誠度無能為，即謾書謝監軍，求洗前咎。

translations.literal: Shaocheng judged that nothing could be done, and at once sent a deceitful letter thanking the army supervisor and asking to wash away former faults.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng judged that Quanyi could do nothing more and at once sent a deceitful letter thanking the army supervisor and asking to be forgiven his former faults.

sentences.zh: 帝下其議，宰相賈耽以為五樓之敗，賊不追者，以冀恩耳，請納其誠。

translations.literal: The Emperor submitted it for discussion; Chancellor Jia Dan thought that at the defeat at Wulou the rebels did not pursue because they hoped for favor; he requested accepting their sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor submitted it for discussion; Chancellor Jia Dan argued that at the defeat at Wulou the rebels had not pursued because they hoped for imperial favor, and he requested accepting their sincerity.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 全義班師，過闕下，托疾不入謁。

translations.literal: Quanyi withdrew the army, passed below the palace gates, feigned illness and did not enter for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi withdrew the army, passed below the palace gates, feigned illness, and did not enter for an audience.

sentences.zh: 司馬崔放見帝，謝無功。

translations.literal: Staff officer Cui Fang saw the Emperor and apologized for achieving no merit.
translations.idiomatic: His staff officer Cui Fang saw the emperor and apologized for achieving no merit.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「全義誘少誠歸國，功大矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Quanyi enticed Shaocheng to return to the state—the merit is great!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Quanyi enticed Shaocheng to return to allegiance—the merit is great!

sentences.zh: 何必殺敵乃為功邪？」

translations.literal: Why must killing enemies be merit?"
translations.idiomatic: Why must killing enemies alone count as merit?"

sentences.zh: 還屯夏州，中人即第宴賚，然卒不見天子去。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison at Xiazhou; eunuchs at once feasted and rewarded him at his residence, yet in the end he departed without seeing the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to garrison at Xiazhou; eunuchs at once feasted and rewarded him at his residence, yet in the end he departed without ever seeing the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 時恨帝失政，使奸人得肆雲。

translations.literal: At the time people resented that the Emperor had lost proper government and allowed wicked men to spread freely.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people resented that the emperor had lost proper government and allowed wicked men to spread freely.

sentences.zh: 憲宗在藩，疾之，既嗣位，全義大懼，願入覲，不復用，以太子少保致仕卒。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was in the princely establishment he detested him; once he succeeded to the throne, Quanyi was greatly afraid, wished to enter for audience, was not again employed, and died after retiring as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong was still heir apparent he detested him; once he succeeded to the throne, Quanyi was greatly afraid and wished to enter for an audience, but was not again employed and died after retiring as grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其子獻女樂八人，帝不納，曰：「我方以儉治天下，惡用是為？」

translations.literal: His son presented eight female musicians; the Emperor did not accept them, saying: "I am just now governing the realm with frugality—what use is there for this?"
translations.idiomatic: His son presented eight female musicians; the emperor did not accept them, saying, "I am just now governing the realm with frugality—what use is there for this?"

sentences.zh: 盧從史，其先在元魏時為盛族，後徙籍不常。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi, his forebears in the Northern Wei era were a great clan; later their household registration moved without fixed place.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi's forebears had been a great clan in the Northern Wei era; later their household registration moved without a fixed place.

sentences.zh: 父虔，好學，由進士第歷御史、秘書監。

translations.literal: His father Qian loved learning, passed the jinshi examination, and served as Censor and Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian loved learning, passed the jinshi examination, and served as censor and director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 從史少好騎射，遊澤、潞間，節度使李長榮署為督將。

translations.literal: Congshi in youth loved riding and archery, wandered between Ze and Lu, and Military Governor Li Changrong appointed him supervising general.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi in his youth loved riding and archery, wandered between Ze and Lu, and military governor Li Changrong appointed him supervising general.

sentences.zh: 貞元後，蕃臣缺，德宗必取本軍所喜戴者授之。

translations.literal: After Zhenyuan, when frontier military commissioners were vacant, Dezong always took whomever the native army delighted in and honored and gave the post to him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhenyuan era, when military commissioner posts on the frontier fell vacant, Dezong always appointed whomever the native army delighted in and honored.

sentences.zh: 從史在潞，奸獪得士心，又善附迎中人，會長榮卒，即擢拜昭義節度副大使。

translations.literal: Congshi was at Lu, crafty and cunning in winning soldiers' hearts, and also skilled at attaching himself to and welcoming eunuchs; when Changrong died, he was at once promoted to Zhaoyi Deputy Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi was at Lu, crafty and cunning in winning the soldiers' hearts and skilled at attaching himself to eunuchs; when Changrong died, he was at once promoted to Zhaoyi deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既得誌，浸恣不道，至奪部將妻，而能辯給粉澤其非。

translations.literal: Once he had his wish, he gradually indulged in unbridled conduct, even seizing his officers' wives, yet could argue fluently and whitewash his wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had his wish, he gradually indulged in unbridled conduct, even seizing his officers' wives, yet could argue fluently and whitewash his wrongs.

sentences.zh: 府屬孔戡等屢以直語爭刺，初唯唯，後益不從，皆引去。

translations.literal: Staff member Kong Kan and others repeatedly used blunt words to dispute and criticize him; at first he assented vaguely, later increasingly did not follow them, and all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: His staff member Kong Kan and others repeatedly used blunt words to dispute and criticize him; at first he assented vaguely, later increasingly ignored them, and all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元和中，丁父喪未官，從史即獻計誅王承宗，陰向帝旨，繇是奪服，復領澤、潞。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, while in mourning for his father and not yet in office, Congshi at once offered a plan to execute Wang Chengzong, secretly aligned with the Emperor's intent; thereby he was released from mourning garments and again took command of Ze and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, while still in mourning for his father and not yet in office, Congshi at once offered a plan to execute Wang Chengzong, secretly aligning with the emperor's intent; thereby he was released from mourning garments and again took command of Ze and Lu.

sentences.zh: 因詔討賊，而勒兵逗留，陰與承宗交，得其密號授軍中，又高芻粟直以售度支。

translations.literal: By edict he was to attack rebels, yet he held his troops and lingered, secretly communicating with Chengzong, obtaining his secret signals and giving them to the army, and also raised the price of fodder grain to sell to the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was to attack the rebels, yet he held his troops and lingered, secretly communicating with Chengzong, obtaining his secret signals and passing them to the army, and also raised the price of fodder grain to sell to the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 即上書求兼宰相，且誣諸軍與賊通，兵未可進。

translations.literal: He at once memorialized requesting to be concurrent chancellor, and also slandered the various armies as communicating with rebels, saying the troops could not yet advance.
translations.idiomatic: He at once memorialized requesting to serve concurrently as chancellor and slandered the various armies as communicating with the rebels, saying the troops could not yet advance.

sentences.zh: 憲宗患之。

translations.literal: Xianzong was troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was troubled by him.

sentences.zh: 初，神策中尉吐突承璀與對壘，從史時過其營飲博，承璀多出寶帶、奇玩誇之。

translations.literal: At first Shence Commandant Tuoba Chenghuan was encamped opposite him; Congshi would visit his camp to drink and gamble; Chenghuan often produced precious belts and curious objects to show off to him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shence commandant Tutu Chengcui was encamped opposite him; Congshi would visit his camp to drink and gamble, and Chengcui often produced precious belts and curious objects to show off to him.

sentences.zh: 從史資沓猥，所玩悅必遺焉。

translations.literal: Congshi's means were mean and paltry; whatever pleased him he would certainly give away to Chenghuan.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi's means were mean and paltry; whatever pleased him he would certainly give away to Chenghuan.

sentences.zh: 從史喜，益狎不疑。

translations.literal: Congshi was pleased and grew still more familiar without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi was pleased and grew still more familiar without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 帝用裴垍謀，敕承璀圖之。

translations.literal: The Emperor used Pei Ji's plan and ordered Chenghuan to scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor used Pei Ji's plan and ordered Chenghuan to scheme against him.

sentences.zh: 承璀伏壯士幕下，伺其來與語，士突起捽持出帳後，縛內車中。

translations.literal: Chenghuan hid strong men beneath his tent; when Congshi came to converse, the men suddenly rose, seized and dragged him out behind the tent, bound him, and put him inside a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghuan hid strong men beneath his tent; when Congshi came to converse, the men suddenly rose, seized him, dragged him out behind the tent, bound him, and put him inside a carriage.

sentences.zh: 從者驚亂，斬數十人，諭以密詔，而大將烏重胤素忠果，部勒其眾，乃定。

translations.literal: His followers were alarmed and in disorder; several tens were beheaded; they were instructed with the secret edict; but the great general Wu Zhongyin was by nature loyal and resolute and marshaled his troops, and then it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: His followers were alarmed and in disorder; several tens were beheaded and instructed with the secret edict, but the great general Wu Zhongyin, who was by nature loyal and resolute, marshaled the troops, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 會夜，疾驅，未明出境，道路無知者。

translations.literal: It happened to be night; they drove swiftly; before dawn they left the border; no one on the roads knew.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be night; they drove swiftly and, before dawn, left the border without anyone on the roads knowing.

sentences.zh: 於是五年夏四月，有詔慰其軍，疏從史罪惡，貶州司馬，賜死。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the fifth year, fourth month of summer, there was an edict to comfort his army, set forth Congshi's crimes, demoted him to prefectural staff officer, and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon in the fifth year, fourth month of summer, an edict comforted his army, set forth Congshi's crimes, demoted him to prefectural staff officer, and granted him death.

sentences.zh: 子繼宗等並徙嶺南。

translations.literal: His sons Jizong and the rest were all banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jizong and the rest were all banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 高霞寓，幽州范陽人。

translations.literal: Gao Xiayu, a man of Fanyang in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiayu was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 其先五代不異居，孝聞裏閭。

translations.literal: His forebears for five generations did not live apart; their filial piety was heard in the lanes and hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears for five generations had not lived apart, and their filial piety was renowned in the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 德宗初，采訪使洪經綸言之，詔表闕於門。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dezong's reign, Investigation Commissioner Hong Jinglun spoke of this; an edict set up a commemorative arch at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dezong's reign, investigation commissioner Hong Jinglun spoke of this, and an edict set up a commemorative arch at the gate.

sentences.zh: 霞寓能讀《春秋》及兵法，頗以感概自尚，狡譎多變。

translations.literal: Xiayu could read the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 and military manuals, prided himself considerably on passionate resolve, and was crafty and changeable.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayu could read the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 and military manuals, prided himself on passionate resolve, and was crafty and changeable.

sentences.zh: 往見長武城使高崇文，崇文異其才，檄任軍職。

translations.literal: He went to see Changwu Fort commander Gao Chongwen; Chongwen was struck by his talent and summoned him to a military post.
translations.idiomatic: He went to see Changwu Fort commander Gao Chongwen; Chongwen was struck by his talent and summoned him to a military post.

sentences.zh: 從擊劉辟，戰輒克，下鹿頭城，降李文悅、仇良輔等，追戰七盤城有功，禽辟於羊灌。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Liu Pi, in battle he always prevailed; he took Lutou City, received the surrender of Li Wenyue, Qiu Liangfu, and others, had merit in pursuit battle at Qipan City, and captured Pi at Yangguan.
translations.idiomatic: Following the campaign against Liu Pi, he always prevailed in battle; he took Lutou City, received the surrender of Li Wenyue, Qiu Liangfu, and others, distinguished himself in pursuit at Qipan City, and captured Pi at Yangguan.

sentences.zh: 擢拜彭州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Prefect of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted and appointed prefect of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄代崇文為長武城使，封感義郡王。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Chongwen as Changwu Fort commander and was enfeoffed Prince of Ganyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Chongwen as Changwu Fort commander and was enfeoffed as Prince of Ganyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 元和中，以左威衛將軍隨吐突承璀討王承宗，諸將多覆軍，獨霞寓有功，詔藏所獲鎧仗於神策庫以旌之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, as Left Weiwu Guard General he followed Tuoba Chenghuan to attack Wang Chengzong; many generals lost their armies, but Xiayu alone had merit; an edict stored the armor and weapons he captured in the Shence arsenal to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, as left Weiwu guard general he followed Tutu Chengcui to attack Wang Chengzong; many generals lost their armies, but Xiayu alone distinguished himself, and an edict stored the armor and weapons he captured in the Shence arsenal to honor him.

sentences.zh: 承璀已執盧從史，其軍相驚，乃遣霞寓諭之，麾而大呼曰：「元惡縛矣，公等宜自安！」

translations.literal: Chenghuan had already seized Lu Congshi; his army was mutually alarmed; he therefore sent Xiayu to instruct them, waving his hand and shouting loudly: "The chief villain is bound—you gentlemen should settle yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Chenghuan had already seized Lu Congshi, and Congshi's army was alarmed; he therefore sent Xiayu to instruct them, waving his hand and shouting loudly, "The chief villain is bound—you gentlemen should settle yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 即脫鎧揖而前，眾遂定，欲留為帥，霞寓間道去。

translations.literal: He at once removed his armor, bowed, and advanced; the masses then settled; they wished to keep him as commander, but Xiayu left by a hidden route.
translations.idiomatic: He at once removed his armor, bowed, and advanced; the troops then settled down; they wished to keep him as commander, but Xiayu left by a hidden route.

sentences.zh: 拜豐州刺史、三城都團練防禦使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Fengzhou and Defender-in-Chief of the Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Fengzhou and defender-in-chief of the Three Cities.

sentences.zh: 討吳元濟也，析山南東道為兩鎮，以霞寓宿將，拜唐鄧隋節度使，遏賊南沖。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Wu Yuanji, Shannan East Route was divided into two commands; because Xiayu was a veteran general, he was appointed Military Governor of Tang-Deng-Sui to block the rebels' southern thrust.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Wu Yuanji, Shannan East Route was divided into two commands; because Xiayu was a veteran general, he was appointed military governor of Tang-Deng-Sui to block the rebels' southern thrust.

sentences.zh: 霞寓雖悍，而寡謀，統制尤非所善，始引兵趨蕭陂，戰小勝，進至文城柵，賊偽北，逐之，為伏所掩，遂大敗，才以身免。

translations.literal: Xiayu, though fierce, was poor in planning and especially unskilled in command and control; he first led troops toward Xiaobo, won a small victory, advanced to Wencheng Stockade; the rebels feigned retreat northward; he pursued and was caught by an ambush; he suffered a great defeat and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayu, though fierce, was poor in planning and especially unskilled in command; he first led troops toward Xiaobo and won a small victory, then advanced to Wencheng Stockade; the rebels feigned a retreat northward, he pursued them into an ambush, suffered a great defeat, and barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 詒貶歸州刺史。

translations.literal: By edict he was demoted to Prefect of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was demoted to prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 乃厚賂權宦，召為右衛大將軍，拜振武節度使。

translations.literal: He then bribed powerful eunuchs heavily, was recalled as Right Guard Grand General, and appointed Military Governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: He then bribed powerful eunuchs heavily, was recalled as right guard grand general, and appointed military governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃攻鹽、豐二州，霞寓以兵五千屯拂雲堆，虜引去。

translations.literal: It happened the Tibetans attacked Yan and Feng prefectures; Xiayu with five thousand troops camped at Fuyun Mound; the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans attacked Yan and Feng prefectures, Xiayu camped five thousand troops at Fuyun Mound and the barbarians withdrew.

sentences.zh: 浚金河，溉鹵地數千頃。

translations.literal: He dredged the Golden River and irrigated several thousand qing of saline land.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the Golden River and irrigated several thousand qing of saline land.

sentences.zh: 改左武衛大將軍，又節度邠寧，位檢校司徒。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Wuwei Guard Grand General, again commanded Binning, and held the post of Acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to left Wuwei guard grand general, again commanded Binning, and held the post of acting minister of education.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，疽發首，不能事，以右金吾衛大將軍召，卒於道，贈太保。

translations.literal: In the Baoli era, an abscess broke out on his head and he could not attend to affairs; he was recalled as Right Golden Crow Guard Grand General, died on the road, and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoli era an abscess broke out on his head and he could not attend to affairs; he was recalled as right Golden Crow guard grand general, died on the road, and was posthumously made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 霞寓位既高，言多不遜，帝欲罷其兵，益自憂，乃上私第為佛祠，請署曰「懷恩」，以塞帝疑。

translations.literal: Once Xiayu's position was high, his words were often disrespectful; the Emperor wished to remove his troops; he grew still more anxious himself; he therefore built a Buddhist shrine at his private residence and requested it be inscribed "Cherishing Grace" to block the Emperor's suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiayu's position was high, his words were often disrespectful; the emperor wished to remove his troops; he grew still more anxious and built a Buddhist shrine at his private residence, requesting it be inscribed "Cherishing Grace" to allay the emperor's suspicions.

sentences.zh: 俄又詺侮僚屬，作慢語斥訕大臣，其反覆自任類此。

translations.literal: Soon he again insulted and reviled his staff, composed contemptuous words to denounce great ministers—his capricious self-will was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again insulted his staff and composed contemptuous words denouncing great ministers; his capricious self-will was of this sort.
